findings.title: validateHandlerOrder pricing bounds bypass via computeRatioX96 overflow (sqrtPriceX96=0)
confidence_deductions: Requires CLOB handler relying on validateHandlerOrder (-10)
Bounded to token pairs with max-only pricing bounds (-5)
findings.description: When SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 overflows (extreme amount ratios), it returns 0. In validateHandlerOrder (AMMStandardHook.sol:215-223), the max price check evaluates '0 > maxSqrtPriceX96' which is always false, so astronomical-price orders pass validation despite max bounds being configured. In contrast, _validatePricingBounds (line 847) explicitly checks sqrtPriceX96==0 and reverts. This asymmetry means CLOB handler orders bypass max pricing bounds when the price ratio overflows.
findings.impact: Token creators who set max pricing bounds to protect against extreme-price CLOB orders get no protection when the price ratio is so extreme it overflows. A CLOB maker could fill orders at astronomical prices.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Token admin sets max pricing bounds (min=0, max=1e30) synced to hook. 2. Attacker creates CLOB order with amountIn=1, amountOut=type(uint160).max. 3. computeRatioX96 overflows, returns 0. 4. 0 > 1e30 is false, max check passes. 5. Order accepted despite effective price >> max bound.
findings.victim: Token holders protected by pricing bounds
findings.extractable_value: Depends on CLOB order size and price deviation
attack_sequence: Token admin sets max-only pricing bounds on hook
Attacker creates CLOB order with extreme price ratio causing overflow
computeRatioX96 returns 0 due to uint160 overflow
validateHandlerOrder max check passes (0 > max is false)
Order accepted at price exceeding configured maximum

findings.title: setTokenSettings syncs original settings (initialized=false) to hooks instead of memSettings
confidence_deductions: Impact is auto-refetch rather than fund loss (-15)
findings.description: In CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.setTokenSettings (line 397), the sync loop calls registryUpdateTokenSettings(token, settings) with the ORIGINAL settings parameter, not memSettings (which has initialized=true set at line 377). The hook stores initialized=false. On next swap, _getOrFetchTokenSettings sees initialized=false and re-fetches from registry, silently overriding synced settings with latest registry state. This breaks the intended push-based cache model.
findings.impact: Token admin syncs specific settings to hook, then changes registry settings without hook sync. Hook auto-refetches and picks up the unsynced changes, breaking the admin's intended per-hook isolation.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Admin calls setTokenSettings(fees=500BPS, hooksToSync=[hook]). Hook caches with initialized=false. 2. Admin calls setTokenSettings(fees=0, hooksToSync=[]). 3. Next swap: hook sees initialized=false, re-fetches, gets 0 fees.
findings.victim: Token admin expecting cached settings isolation
findings.extractable_value: Indirect - enables fee bypass if admin sequence exploitable
attack_sequence: Admin syncs settings with 500BPS fee to hook (initialized=false propagated)
Admin updates registry to 0 fees without re-syncing hook
Next swap triggers auto-refetch, hook gets 0 fees instead of synced 500BPS
prerequisites: Admin changes settings after initial sync without re-syncing
code_smells: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol:397 - syncs settings instead of memSettings
findings.what_remains_unverified: Whether this can be weaponized for direct fund extraction (likely Low impact)

findings.title: Unsynced pricing bounds in validateHandlerOrder silently skip all price validation
confidence_deductions: Requires admin not syncing bounds to specific hook (-10)
Impact depends on handler reliance on this validation (-10)
findings.description: validateHandlerOrder reads pricing bounds from hook's local _pricingBounds cache (line 210). Unlike _getOrFetchTokenSettings (which auto-fetches), _pricingBounds has NO auto-fetch mechanism - it is purely push-based via registryUpdatePricingBounds. If bounds are set in registry but never synced to a specific hook, the hook's isSet=false, and validation is silently skipped. A CLOB handler relying on this hook for order validation accepts orders at any price.
findings.impact: CLOB orders bypass price validation when pricing bounds exist in registry but weren't synced to the specific hook instance
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Admin sets tight pricing bounds in registry (min=1e18, max=2e18) without syncing to hook. 2. Attacker calls validateHandlerOrder with extreme price. 3. Hook has no cached bounds, isSet=false, validation skipped.
findings.victim: Users of CLOB handler expecting price protection
findings.extractable_value: Depends on CLOB order execution without price protection
attack_sequence: Admin sets pricing bounds in registry without syncing to specific hook
Attacker submits CLOB order with price outside intended bounds
Hook silently skips validation (no cached bounds)
prerequisites: Pricing bounds not synced to specific hook instance
code_smells: AMMStandardHook.sol:210 - no auto-fetch for pricing bounds unlike token settings
findings.what_remains_unverified: Whether any deployed CLOB handler relies on this validation path

findings.title: Whitelist ID change via registryUpdateTokenSettings leaves hook with empty whitelist, blocking direct swaps
confidence_deductions: Impact is DoS not fund extraction (-15)
Admin can fix by syncing whitelist content (-5)
findings.description: When setTokenSettings changes pairedTokenWhitelistId from 1 to 2 and syncs to hook, only _tokenSettings is updated via registryUpdateTokenSettings. The hook's _pairTokenWhitelists[2] remains empty because whitelist CONTENT is synced separately. For direct swaps (poolId==0), _validateTokenTradingRules checks _pairTokenWhitelists[newId].contains(pairedToken), which fails for all tokens. This creates asymmetric DoS: direct swaps break while pool swaps continue unaffected.
findings.impact: All direct swaps for the token fail until admin separately syncs whitelist 2 content to hook
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Token has whitelist 1 with WETH, synced to hook. 2. Admin changes to whitelist 2 via setTokenSettings(hooksToSync=[hook]). 3. Hook has pairedTokenWhitelistId=2 but _pairTokenWhitelists[2] is empty. 4. Direct swap with WETH reverts PairNotAllowed.
findings.victim: Direct swap users of the affected token
attack_sequence: Admin syncs whitelist 1 content and settings to hook
Admin changes settings to reference whitelist 2 and syncs settings to hook
Admin forgets to separately sync whitelist 2 content
All direct swaps fail with PairNotAllowed
prerequisites: Admin changes whitelist ID without syncing new whitelist content
code_smells: AMMStandardHook.sol:522 - settings update doesn't trigger whitelist content sync
findings.what_remains_unverified: Whether this is considered by-design (documented desync model)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-HR-03: disabled pool bypass via cache desync
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When initialized=false is propagated (H-R3-HR-01), _getOrFetchTokenSettings auto-refetches, picking up checkDisabledPools=true. When auto-cached with initialized=true, cache persists but admin can re-sync. The attack window requires admin to update registry without syncing AND auto-cache to not have occurred. Narrow preconditions make this impractical.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-HR-04: auto-cache leaves whitelist empty (DoS for new tokens)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Auto-cache stores settings but not whitelist content. However, if pairedTokenWhitelistId > 0 and content not synced, direct swaps fail. This is IDENTICAL to EH-004 (H-R3-HR-05) and documented as intentional desync model in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry NatSpec. The registry docs explicitly state hooks maintain independent caches and content sync is separate.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-HR-06: auto-fetch race condition (front-running token initialization)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Front-runner can trigger auto-cache of initial settings before admin syncs. However, admin's subsequent registryUpdateTokenSettings always overwrites the hook cache regardless of initialized flag. The race window exists but the admin's sync always wins. At worst, one swap executes at initial settings before admin sync arrives.

Tstorish _onTstoreSupportActivated copies sstore slot to tstore atomically (AMMStandardHook.sol:951-954). Function pointers in Tstorish are immutable but the fallback functions dynamically check tstoreSupport. Value is preserved across activation. No desync possible.

validateAddLiquidity checks price BEFORE liquidity is added. For concentrated liquidity pools (DynamicPoolType), adding liquidity proportionally doesn't change the pool price. For FixedPoolType, price is fixed. For SingleProviderPoolType, price is hook-controlled. No pool type in scope allows single-sided liquidity addition that shifts price. Additionally, validateAddLiquidity is AMM-only (guard blocks external callers).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Reentrancy via malicious token callback during PermitC transfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All AMM entry points protected by TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags. ENTERED bit prevents reentry. Hook functions additionally require msg.sender == AMM. External callers blocked by _requireCallerIsAMM guard.

AMMStandardHook doesn't maintain separate balance accounting. It writes transient storage (direct swap amount) and caches settings, both of which are reverted atomically if the AMM transaction reverts. No persistent desync possible between hook and pool state. Registry updates require _requireCallerIsRegistry guard.

AMMStandardHook uses exactly ONE transient storage slot: DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT. Written only in beforeSwap, read only in afterSwap. No other operation (addLiquidity, removeLiquidity, collectFees, validateHandlerOrder) accesses this slot. No cross-path tstore leak possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-03: output swap fee amplification with high hopFeeBPS
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside extension-hijacker primary scope (fee path, not extension point). Noted for price-distorter/precision-sniper agents. The fee amplification at AMMModule.sol:2818-2822 is real but requires fee manager to set hopFeeBPS=9999 which is a privileged admin action.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-05: non-token hook fee key asymmetry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside extension-hijacker primary scope. The key asymmetry in _storeNonTokenHookFees (tokenFor, tokenFor) vs _transferHookFeesByHook (tokenFor, tokenFee) only matters when tokenFor != tokenFee, which doesn't occur in normal flow. Hook developers querying getHookFeesOwedByHook with wrong parameters is an API usability issue, not a vulnerability.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-06: flags cleared before transfer handler callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: After _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers clears custom flags (line 3190), _executeTransferHandlerCallback runs without SWAP_GUARD_FLAG. However, transfer handlers don't check SWAP_GUARD_FLAG for authorization. CLOBTransferHandler and PermitTransferHandler use their own validation. No handler in scope relies on checkAMMExecutionState for security decisions.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-01: 100% dynamic fee on input swaps (off-by-one)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside extension-hijacker primary scope (fee validation). The asymmetric check at line 1717 (input: > MAX_BPS, output: >= MAX_BPS) allows 100% fee on input swaps. However, pool fee is set by pool hook (malicious hook = Tier B). Also limitAmount check protects users. SqrtPriceCalculator computes correctly for normal values.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-07: input swap min protocol fee amplification
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside extension-hijacker primary scope (fee math). The amplification at AMMModule.sol:2657-2661 occurs when poolFeeBPS * lpFeeBPS approaches DOUBLE_BPS. This amplification reduces swapAmountIn (not inflates it), meaning the user gets less output. The limitAmount check at line 2171 protects users who set reasonable slippage.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-DP-09: output swap partial fill overcharges hook fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside extension-hijacker primary scope (pool type interaction). Output hook fees are applied before pool call, but partial fills at lines 1569-1577 adjust amountOut and re-compute. The _applySwapByOutputOutputFees stores fees based on the PRE-adjustment amount. Whether this is a real overcharge depends on exact execution ordering. Noted as lead for precision-sniper.

theft_theses.thesis: Overflow in computeRatioX96 bypasses max pricing bounds in validateHandlerOrder, allowing CLOB orders at extreme prices
theft_theses.victim: Token holders protected by pricing bounds
theft_theses.asset: Trading protection (indirect fund impact via extreme-price orders)

theft_theses.thesis: Settings sync propagates initialized=false, breaking cache model for subsequent registry changes
theft_theses.victim: Token admin expecting cached settings isolation
theft_theses.asset: Fee protection (indirect - unsynced fee changes take effect)

theft_theses.thesis: Unsynced pricing bounds silently skip all CLOB order price validation
theft_theses.victim: Users relying on handler order price protection

theft_theses.thesis: Whitelist ID change without content sync blocks all direct swaps (DoS)

hypothesis_results.detail: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow. validateHandlerOrder checks 0 > max which is false. Max bound bypassed. _validatePricingBounds has explicit sqrtPriceX96==0 check but validateHandlerOrder does not.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If computeRatioX96 were to revert on overflow (like _validatePricingBounds checks), the bypass would be impossible. But it returns 0 to signal overflow, and validateHandlerOrder doesn't check for this signal.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:221 (max check only, no zero check)

hypothesis_results.detail: Line 397 syncs `settings` (initialized=false from caller) not `memSettings` (initialized=true from line 377). Hook cache has initialized=false, triggering auto-refetch on next access.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If registryUpdateTokenSettings explicitly set initialized=true on the received settings before storing, the cache would be stable. But it stores whatever the registry sends.

hypothesis_results.detail: H-R3-HR-01 (initialized=false) causes auto-refetch which picks up the correct checkDisabledPools setting. Cache-only scenario requires auto-cache first (initialized=true), then admin changes without sync. Narrow window, not profitable.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If admin updates checkDisabledPools=true and disables pool without syncing hook, hook's stale cache (checkDisabledPools=false) would skip the check. But auto-refetch from H-R3-HR-01 makes this unreliable.

hypothesis_results.detail: Auto-cache with empty whitelists is identical to H-R3-HR-05 and is documented as intentional desync behavior. Registry NatSpec explicitly states hooks maintain independent caches.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: Auto-cache stores settings with whitelist IDs but no content. If admin relies on auto-cache without explicit content sync, direct swaps fail. But this is documented behavior.

hypothesis_results.detail: Changing pairedTokenWhitelistId via setTokenSettings only updates _tokenSettings, not _pairTokenWhitelists content. Hook references new ID with empty content set. Direct swaps fail.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If registryUpdateTokenSettings also triggered whitelist content sync for the new ID, the desync wouldn't occur. But it only updates the settings struct.

hypothesis_results.detail: Admin's registryUpdateTokenSettings always overwrites hook cache, winning the race. At worst one swap at initial settings before sync.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: Front-runner triggers auto-cache before admin sync. Admin's sync via registryUpdateTokenSettings overwrites regardless of initialized flag.

hypothesis_results.detail: Tstorish activation copies sstore to tstore atomically. Value preserved. Function pointers check tstoreSupport dynamically.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: _onTstoreSupportActivated uses assembly tstore(slot, sload(slot)) which atomically copies the value. No gap possible.

hypothesis_results.detail: Pool types in scope don't allow price-changing single-sided liquidity addition. DynamicPoolType adds proportionally. FixedPoolType is fixed-price. SingleProviderPoolType is hook-priced. AMM guard blocks external callers from validateAddLiquidity.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a pool type allowed single-sided addition that shifts price, the TOCTOU gap between validateAddLiquidity price check and actual addition would matter.

hypothesis_results.detail: Pricing bounds use push-only sync (no auto-fetch). Bounds set in registry but not synced to hook are invisible. validateHandlerOrder silently skips validation.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If _pricingBounds had auto-fetch like _getOrFetchTokenSettings, unsynced bounds would still be enforced. But pricing bounds have no auto-fetch mechanism.

hypothesis_results.detail: Outside primary scope (fee validation not extension point). Asymmetric fee check allows 100% on input swaps. Requires malicious pool hook (Tier B). limitAmount protects users.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If poolFeeBPS check used >= for both input and output, 100% fee would be blocked on input swaps too.

hypothesis_results.detail: Outside primary scope. Fee amplification requires admin to set extreme hopFeeBPS. Admin-controlled configuration, not exploitable by external attacker.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If hopFeeBPS were capped lower (e.g., 5000), the amplification factor would be bounded. But max 9999 creates up to 10000x amplification.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:3486 (hopFeeBPS < MAX_BPS check allows up to 9999)

hypothesis_results.detail: Outside primary scope. Key asymmetry exists but doesn't affect normal flow where tokenFor==tokenFee.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a hook developer queries with (tokenA, tokenB), they get 0 instead of actual fees. But correct query is (tokenA, tokenA).

hypothesis_results.detail: Flags cleared before handler callback but no handler checks SWAP_GUARD_FLAG for authorization.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a future transfer handler used checkAMMExecutionState(SWAP_GUARD_FLAG) for security, it would see incorrect state. But no current handler does.

hypothesis_results.detail: Outside primary scope. Fee amplification reduces swapAmountIn, protected by limitAmount check.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If limitAmount is set to type(uint256).max by user, the amplified fee deduction would pass. But users setting infinite slippage accept this risk.

hypothesis_results.detail: Outside primary scope. Partial fill hook fee overcharge needs deeper analysis of execution ordering in _poolSwapByOutput.
hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If output hook fees were recalculated after partial fill adjustment, overcharge would be eliminated.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:1576-1577 (adjustedAmountSpecified recalculated but hook fees not)
